chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore her master a child), when her master dies and had bequeathed to her, he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is emancipated within the one-third share, and for her is the bequest.'

key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ: Umm al-Walad: A female slave who bore her master a child, who becomes free upon his death.
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The third: The portion of the estate (one-third) available for bequests after debts and heirs are accounted for.
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: The bequest: A gift left in a will to someone who is not a fixed heir.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a concubine who bore a child when her master dies and bequeathed to her?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the emancipation of an Umm al-Walad is treated as a bequest drawn from the one-third share of the estate, ensuring her freedom does not encroach upon the fixed shares of heirs. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that manumission is a voluntary act of wealth distribution, distinct from the mandatory inheritance portions, thereby balancing the master's discretion with the concubine's right to freedom upon his death.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>
regarding a mother of a child, when her master dies from her, and had bequeathed to her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is emancipated with regards to the third, and for her is the bequest’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from those whom he has mentioned who have narrated the following: “About the case of the mother of a child, when her master dies who has made a will for her, abu al- Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘She becomes free in one-third and the will belongs to her.’”
